main_text.head: DE PHYSICA.
main_text.p: PHYSICA, die natursunst/est ars bene naturam cognoscendi. Ejus subjectum est natura ipsa.
Substantia est subsistentia, à naturæ Conditore, summè bono (tantùm enim ex naturæ lumine de Deo cognosci potest) nempe ente entium creata. Estq; aut spiritualis aut corporea.
Spiritualis substantia est immortalis, intelligentia ac voluntate prædita.
Intelligentia est facultas spirituum, qua pro suo captu omnia entia intelligunt.
Voluntas est facultas spirituum, qua liberrimè entia eligunt aut rejiciunt.
Spiritualis est substantia Geniorum & Animarum hominum.
Genii sunt boni vel mali. Hoc ex naturæ lumine veteres perspexerunt: ideoq; unicuiq; duos assignârunt Genios, bonum & malum.
Anima hominis est substantia spiritualis primùm à numine homini inspirata: Deinde ex propagatione naturali à parentibus in liberos tradùcta, & tanquam lumen de lumine accensa.
Judicium animæ vel simplex est vel compositum.
Simplex est, quo res ipsas vel rerum affectiones simpliciter perpendit.
Compositum judicium est, quo ex simplicibus rebus dispositis aliquid colligit.

page.notes: Engraved decorative initial "D" at the start of "Dhysica" (printed as the woodcut initial P-shaped ornament; read as "PHYSICA", joined to the first word). Printed page number "325" at the top. Mixed long s and round s are normalised to plain s as required. Words such as "substantia" are copied with long s as printed; rule-compliant plain-s rendering is applied where the text is set in roman. Some letters in the scan are doubtful: "natursunst/est" may be a printer's error or a rendering of "natur-" with a slash; "Geniorum" and "assignârunt" are as printed. The "x 3" at the foot is a gathering signature.
